<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This file is a standard `.gitignore` for an AUR package. It uses the pattern `*` to ignore all files, then explicitly unignores the essential packaging files: `.gitignore`, `.SRCINFO`, `PKGBUILD`, `noaidarling-git.install`, and `dkms.conf`. There are no network requests, no obfuscated or encoded commands, no dangerous functions like `eval` or `base64`, and no unexpected file operations. The content is consistent with ordinary AUR packaging hygiene and serves only to ensure packaging files are tracked by git while other files are gitignored. No supply-chain attack indicators are present.
</details>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The file is a .SRCINFO metadata file for the noaidarling-extra-git AUR package. It contains only package description, dependencies, source URLs (all git+https from the NoAiDarling GitHub organization), and md5sums set to SKIP, which is standard for VCS sources. There are no build scripts, eval, base64, curl, wget, or any executable code present. The source entries reference the upstream project's repositories, and the SKIP checksums are required for mutable git branches. No suspicious network downloads, obfuscated commands, or unexpected file operations are evident. The packaging follows normal AUR conventions for a large collection of git components.
</details>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a split-package VCS PKGBUILD for NoAiDarling, a macOS compatibility layer for Linux. All declared sources originate from the project's own GitHub organization (github.com/NoAiDarling), and the build uses standard tools: git submodules, cmake, make/ninja, and git-lfs for large binary files. Checksums are SKIP, which is required and normal for git sources.

The prepare() function remaps submodule URLs to local clones under $srcdir and updates them via the file:// protocol. This avoids redundant network fetches and keeps submodules consistent with the source array; it does not pull or execute code from unrelated hosts. The build() and package_*() functions run cmake and install component files into $pkgdir, matching ordinary Arch packaging practice.

No data exfiltration, obfuscated code, reverse shells, curl|bash patterns, or unexpected system modifications are present. The behavior is consistent with upstream application functionality and standard AUR workflow.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>
Standard VCS split-package PKGBUILD; no malicious behavior detected.
</summary>
